questions.title: How many sugar types build the ABO antigens
questions.question: How many types of sugar molecules are primarily involved in determining the ABO blood group antigens?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Three sugar types is too few to account for the full ABO antigen family — galactose, fucose and the two N-acetyl amino sugars alone already make four, before the base linking sugar is counted.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Four sugar types omits one of the five monosaccharide building blocks (galactose, fucose, N-acetylglucosamine, N-acetylgalactosamine, and the base linking sugar) that build the ABO antigen family.
explanations.C: Correct. The ABO blood group antigens are branched oligosaccharide chains built from five monosaccharide types: galactose, fucose, N-acetylglucosamine, N-acetylgalactosamine and the base linking sugar. All three ABO phenotypes share the same core chain terminating in fucose (the H antigen); which further single monosaccharide, if any, is added onto that core then sets A, B or O specificity.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Six simple sugars overstates the count; only five monosaccharide types are involved in building the ABO antigen family.

questions.learning_objective: State that five monosaccharide types build the ABO antigen family.
